findings.description: The whole walkway is one 440 m turn rising 110 m (s 400-840), and it is legible from both ends. In the first reveal the viewer sees the complete route and its end as a small wheel and a lollipop 110 m up. In the final 'plunge' frame they see the start of the walk 100 m below while the planet is 600 km down. That is a built-in ruler contradicting the virtual-altitude illusion that beats 5-7 depend on, and it shrinks the cable ('a 100 m drum with a ring around it').
findings.cause: NearRoot (helix, arms, rails, pier) is real 36-146 m geometry and does not take part in the ground-group sink or the virtual altitude. D-035 moved the beads that used to hide the lower turn from the pad.
findings.fix: Beats 6-7: once s > 600, fade NearRoot deck, rail and arm fragments with alpha-to-coverage (the D-042 mechanism) by smoothstep(30 m, 70 m, y_cam - y_frag). The lower turn then dissolves into the sky, sea and Earth drawn behind it, as the ground group did inside the deck. Exclude the cable. Beat 4: the A1 upper veil (y 70-260, s < 400), or re-pose KF4b to yaw 68 and pitch 42 so the pad projects above the top edge (ndc y about +1.14).

findings.description: The D-047 nadir Earth replaced the round-1 'terrazzo' with blurred coffee-stain blobs on cream paper. Every other edge in the film is 1-2 px clean, so the blur reads as a smudge or out-of-focus layer. Defocus is a classic miniature cue (tilt-shift), so the Earth from 600 km reads small and near. Without blue it also does not read as Earth.
findings.cause: The puff and weather mask is evaluated with a wide smoothstep (pre-filtered for aliasing) instead of footprint-sized analytic coverage. Nadir cloud coverage is near 1, so the land shows through as blurred holes and no ocean is visible.
findings.fix: Clamp land and cloud boundary softness to max(1.5 x fwidth, worldSoft / distance), so edges are 1-2 px crisp flat shapes. Lower nadir cloud coverage to about 0.5-0.6 so EARTH_OCEAN appears between puffs and land. Keep the minimum feature size at 40-200 px at 1080p, so continents and weather systems read and the blobs are not stains.

result.overall: Run07 fixes the round's geometric and technical tells: the planet and sun are round (A4), bead silhouettes are smooth (A9), the planet no longer shows stars through it (A10), and the KF6a shadow is now a real leading line (A3). Beat 6 and the final frame now read as intended. The awe deficits that remain are compositional and come from scale logic. (1) Money shot 1 (KF4b) still ends visibly: the one-turn helix reads as a Ferris wheel, the pad as a lollipop and S1 as a ghost dome. (2) Money shot 3's plunge (KF7c) still fails: the cable cones into the deck edge, the helix wheel sits 100 m below and the nadir Earth is blurred stains. The thread can never meet the Earth from the pier, because the nadir is always under the deck. (3) Beat 5's 'land drops away' frames show no object of known size; the KF5c terrace is geometrically hidden at s = 540. (4) The deck-pass horizon (A12) regressed from one seam to a full-width peach band with two seams (S1). (5) Beats 3 and 2 still lack the human-scale cues that were asked for (A8, A6, A15), and the cable still lacks small details (A11). Awe ranking of run07: 1) beat 7 (KF7b, KF7a); 2) beat 6 (KF6a, KF6a2); 3) beat 2 (KF2a strong, KF2b/KF2c weak); 4) beat 4 (lower KF4b strong, top third cluttered); 5) beat 1 (calm by design, but the robes pre-empt beat 2); 6) beat 5 (KF5d improved, KF5a/b/c weak); 7) beat 3 (blinds with no human scale). Weakest compositions in order: KF5c, KF7c, KF5a, KF3, KF5b, KF2b, KF2c. Priority fixes: A12 (seam); A1 and A-r2-1 (veil the near frame above and below the walker); A5 and A-r2-2 (cable aerial fade, crisp Earth, KF7c pitch -45); A2 (re-pose KF5a, re-think KF5c); then A8, A6 with A-r2-3, and A11.

findings.description: Wherever the cable-shadow band crosses shaded (lilac) cloud, a 15-20 px (1080p) strip on each side of the dark core is drawn as fully lit cloud. The band therefore reads as light-dark-light: a dark stripe wrapped in a bleached halo that cuts through the puffs. It looks like a decal composited over the sea, not a shadow falling on it, and it sits on the only leading line of money shot 2.
findings.cause: The band compositing path appears to re-evaluate the cloud colour as lit inside the band's support (core plus 6 m soft edge plus the D-045 widening), for example lerp(litCloud, bandShade, bandAmt), and discards the cloud's own self-shade term there.
findings.fix: Apply the band as a pure multiplier on the already shaded cloud colour: col = shadedCloud * lerp(1, bandTint, 0.8 * bandAmt), or litTotal = min(cloudSelfLit, 1 - 0.8 * bandAmt). Never recompute the lit colour inside the band. Acceptance: on any row crossing the band, no pixel within 40 px of the band axis is brighter than the cloud 40-60 px away on the same side (KF6a y 600/700/780, KF6a2 y 850/950).

findings.evidence: beat06_clouds_KF6a2.png x 300-500 y 880-1020 at 5x: lilac/cream puff boundaries are 1-px stair-steps (about 25-36 codes) with no intermediate values. Count of vertical one-row steps of 12 codes or more in x 0-600 y 700-1000: KF6a2 2799, KF6a 4358, mid 2398. The same jaggies show at 4K: beat06_clouds_KF6a2_4k.png x 2000-2400 y 1500-1900, beat06_clouds_KF6a_4k.png x 700-1500 y 1200-2160. Comparison: run06 beat06_clouds_KF6a.png had a soft marbled sea with no such edges, and the far field (KF6a x 100-400 y 360-480) is properly filtered.
findings.description: The new cumulus-puff cloud sea (D-047) draws its near and mid puff and shade boundaries as unfiltered hard thresholds. Shader-evaluated edges get no MSAA, so every boundary in the lower half of the beat-6 frames is aliased. As the walker climbs and the clouds scroll, these stair-steps will crawl across half the frame of money shot 2 (Part 10 aliasing and shimmer).
findings.cause: step() or a near-zero-width smoothstep on the puff mask and self-shade mask, with no screen-space derivative term; the distance fade only acts far away.
findings.fix: Use smoothstep(t - w, t + w, n) with w = max(w0, 0.75-1.0 x fwidth(n)) on every puff-coverage and puff-shade threshold, and keep the existing far fade. Acceptance: no one-row transition over 12 codes inside the sea in KF6a/KF6a2 at 1080, and a 64x64 crop varies by less than 3 grey levels across a 0.1 px/frame pan.

findings.evidence: beat06_clouds_KF6a2.png: star pixels at full strength inside the bright peach band just above the cloud horizon. findings.description: Stars are drawn at the same +55 to +75 code contrast in the bright twilight glow right down to the limb as in the dark zenith. Over a 0.6-0.7 luma sky they read as dust or dead pixels. At 1-2 px wide they also twinkle (alias) whenever the view pans.
findings.cause: Star intensity is not attenuated by local sky luminance or by elevation above the horizon or limb.
findings.fix: Multiply star brightness by 1 - smoothstep(0.15, 0.35, skyLuma), or fade it over the first 6-10 deg above the limb, and occlude stars inside the ATMO limb ring. Re-check KF6a2 y 380-500: no star more than 10 codes above its background.

findings.description: The edges of a large cast shadow on the terrace show shadow-map texel staircasing smeared by PCF into a sawtooth. In motion (walker plus cascade re-fit) the teeth will crawl along the edge, right where the climb begins.
findings.cause: Cascade resolution is too coarse for this receiver at a grazing sun angle; the cascades are possibly not stable-fit.
findings.fix: Enable stable cascade fitting, raise the main-light shadow map to 4096, or tighten split 0/1 so the terrace within about 60 m of the walker gets texels under 5 cm. Use the high-quality soft-shadow filter. Acceptance: no periodic 4-10 px structure along shadow edges in beat04_tower_end and beat05_spiral_start.

findings.description: The new puff cloud field has no anti-aliasing. Every lit-top/lilac-flank boundary is a hard binary step, and the thin rim crescents break into dashed sub-pixel slivers. findings.description: In the bank direction the horizon is a double line. The sky (with the bank term) is about 10 codes bluer and lighter than the ground directly below it, and about 6 px lower the foot of the bank on the ground makes a second step. In the title/thumbnail shot this draws a thin pale strip between two lines across the full width, against the 'no horizon line' rule (Part 10 items 7/13). It fails 14.5.1 acceptance (2): ground, sky and fog within 1% per channel.
findings.cause: Suspected: sky rays and ground rays composite the bank term and the distance fog differently (bank colour CLOUD_TOP over SKY_H, in a different order or with a different transmittance), so they do not converge at the horizon. The bank's z ramp (225-265 m) projected onto the ground at eye height 1.7 m collapses into 1-2 px.
findings.fix: For ground fragments, evaluate the bank transmittance with the same closed form and composite order as the sky ray (distance fog to SKY_H first, then the bank toward CLOUD_TOP), so that ground at 1 px below the horizon equals sky at 1 px above within 2 codes. Widen the ground-projected bank ramp by the pixel footprint (or start it at z 205) so its foot is at least 6 px soft.

findings.evidence: ThreadConstants.GazeCues with AutoWalker.CinematicPlan (between holds, the gaze returns to yaw 0, pitch 3). Hold ends computed at 0.78x speed: cue 330 (yaw +45) ends at s~336, forward until 345 (~6 s). Cue 345 (+50/+32) ends at ~352, forward until 362 (~7 s). Cue 362 (+58) ends at ~370, forward until 385. Cue 420 (yaw +160) ends at ~426, forward for ~10 s, then cue 440 swings to yaw +150. Pose context: beat04_tower_mid.png is what the forward return shows (the cable pushed to the right edge, x 330-1920).
findings.description: At the first peak, the camera ping-pongs: 45 -> 0 -> 50 -> 0 -> 58 -> 0 -> 30 deg of yaw, looking away from the tower for 6-7 s between each look at it, with pitch dropping from 32 back to 3 between the 'vertigo' cues. That breaks the upward build that beat 4 depends on. In beat 5, the over-the-shoulder look-back does a 160 deg swing back, ~10 s forward, then a 150 deg swing back again. With the 60 deg/s yaw cap, that is roughly 3 s of panning each way, twice, and will read as an indecisive camera in the video.
findings.cause: Cue spacing in s is longer than the hold distance (about 1.17 m/s x hold), so the default forward gaze cuts in between related cues. GazeCue can only interpolate pitch, not yaw.
findings.fix: Chain related cues so that each next cue's s is at or before the previous hold's end. Holds queue, so the next cue then fires directly. Beat 4: (330, +45, +8, 6) -> (336, +50, +8->32, 8) -> (345, +56, +32->50, 10) -> (360, +45, +50->20, 6) -> (385, +30, +12, 4). Beat 5: replace 420/440 with (420, +160, -8, 10) -> (431, +150, -12, 8). Optionally add a yawEnd field to GazeCue for slow pans.

findings.evidence: AutoWalker.cs CinematicPlan.Begin: SlowFactor = max(0.7, 1 - 45 / sum(holds)), with sum(holds) = 206 s over 37 cues, gives a uniform 0.78x at every hold. That adds roughly 8 s to beat 1, 4 s to the beat-3 white, 7.5 s to beat 5 and 5.3 s to the beat-4 reveal.
findings.description: 14.1 asks for slow-downs at the reveals. The budget is instead spread evenly, so the already slow calm and compression beats get as much extra time as the first peak, the emergence onto the cloud sea and the planet.
findings.cause: A single global slow factor.

result.overall: Round 2 fixed or clearly improved the back half of the film. Beat 4's first peak now rises without a cap, the shadow band gives beat 6 a leading line, the planet arrives as an occlusion planetrise, and the final frame is clean. PAC-08, -10, -13 and -14 are fixed; PAC-01 is down to S3. The front half has barely changed. KF1 is pixel-identical in thread contrast and the robes still dominate (PAC-04). The faceless watchers are never seen in beat 2 (PAC-05). The line still disappears for about 140 s (PAC-06). Beat 3 is still about 50 s of treads under white, with only a 1.5% cable ghost at s 305 (PAC-07). Beat 5's land drop still has no anchor (PAC-02: two crack levels now visible, but no terrace or mandala, and a 37 s forward-only stretch). Beat 6's emergence timing (PAC-09, not re-measured), its dazzle (PAC-12) and the bead column, which now reads as a nose cone (PAC-11), are unresolved. The fix wave introduced one blocker: a hard-edged peach band floats across the frame for about 7-8 s on the approach to the cloud deck (PAC-r2-1, a regression from D-037). The gaze schedule also ping-pongs at the first peak and in the beat-5 look-back (PAC-r2-2). The best faceless-watcher image of the run (a hood at eye level beside the tower at s~490) is never framed by a gaze (PAC-r2-3); adding that cue would repair beat 2's missing dread and beat 5's dull middle at once. Estimated curve now: beat 1 awe 5 / calm 6 (target 2/8); beat 2 awe 5 / unease 3-4 (6/6); beat 3 flat (unease ~4 vs 7); beat 4 awe ~9 (10); beat 5 awe ~5 (7); beat 6 awe ~8 (9); beat 7 awe ~9-10 with good relief. Priority: fix PAC-r2-1, chain the beat-4 and beat-5 cues and add the watcher and sun gazes (all cheap ThreadConstants edits), then the beat-1 haze and the bead spacing. Not re-measured, because no run07 sequences exist: PAC-09, PAC-16 and the duration of PAC-r2-1.

(2) Draw every Earth tone edge at width clamp(1.5 x fwidth(n), 0, w_spec), so edges are crisp at any distance and never sub-pixel. (3) Keep continents at 300+ km scale with 2-3 large shapes per view.
